description: The provided image is a 3D bar chart illustrating the accuracy of various large language models across different reasoning types, as evaluated in the paper titled "Are Large Language Models Really Good Logical Reasoners: A Comprehensive Evaluation and Beyond." The horizontal plane of the chart is divided into two axes: the x-axis represents the reasoning types—Inductive, Deductive, and Mix—while the y-axis lists the large language models being compared: Davinci-003, ChatGPT, and BARD. The z-axis, labeled "Accuracy," quantifies the performance of each model on each reasoning type, with values ranging from 0 to 0.6. Each bar is color-coded using a gradient from blue to yellow, where blue represents lower accuracy and yellow represents higher accuracy. The chart shows that all models achieve the highest accuracy on the "Mix" reasoning type, with the "Deductive" reasoning type generally yielding lower accuracy. Among the models, BARD appears to have the highest accuracy across most reasoning types, particularly on the "Mix" category, where its bar reaches the highest point on the chart, approaching an accuracy of 0.6. In contrast, Davinci-003 shows the lowest accuracy, with its bars being the shortest, especially in the "Deductive" and "Inductive" categories. The visual arrangement of the bars, with their varying heights and color gradients, effectively conveys the relative performance of the models, highlighting that while all models perform better on mixed reasoning, their capabilities differ significantly in more specific logical reasoning tasks.
